text:
A: Hello? Oh, hello, love. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes! Hello, I can hear you. I'm Tereza.
A: Julie. Oh, it's nice to finally see you, I saw your photo with all your plants and your calendar, I thought, she looks organised.
B: [laughs] Thank you, I think. Your photo was in the kitchen, with the tea tin. I thought, she looks like she would bring cake.
A: Well, you're not wrong there! I'm always doing flapjacks for the staff room. And a Victoria sponge if someone's leaving.
B: I bake also! Last week I made a cake for my colleague's leaving party. Czech one, with poppy seeds. Everybody looked at it a bit scared, but then they ate everything.
A: Poppy seeds! Oh, I've never had that. Is it nice?
B: Very nice. A little bit sweet, a little bit nutty. My grandmother taught me. She made the best one, I still can't make it like her.
A: Oh, bless her. Is she still with you?
B: No, she died in the pandemic. I couldn't travel back, so I watched the funeral on my phone. Sorry, that's sad.
A: Oh, love, no, don't be sorry. That's awful, not being able to be there. I looked after my mum before she died, she had dementia, and as hard as it was, at least I was with her, you know. I can't imagine being all the way over here.
B: Yes. It's still hard sometimes. My mum also had a health scare last year, so now every time the phone rings late, I worry.
A: Oh, I know that feeling. Is she alright now?
B: Better, yes. I go twice a year. But I'm a terrible flyer, I hold the armrest the whole time.
A: Oh, me too! I check the passports about ten times before we leave. The girls from work took me to Benidorm and I made them get to the airport four hours early.
B: [laughs] Four hours! That's what I would do. My husband says two hours is enough, and I say, Tom, what if there is traffic, what if there is accident on the road?
A: Exactly! Better to be sat there with a coffee than running. What is it you do, love?
B: Clinical trials coordinator, at a hospital in East London. Lots of paperwork, lots of patients, some of them very nervous, so I explain things slowly.
A: Oh, that's like me with my residents. I'm a care assistant. Half of it's just being patient and letting them take their time, isn't it? Sorry, I've gone off on one.
B: No, it's true. I think people forget that part. You must be very good at it.
A: Oh, I don't know about that. I just try. Have you got any little ones?
B: Not yet. Maybe. We are thinking. [laughs] Erm, does that make—
